videoTitle: Why Your Legs Won't Cross (and the 4 Stretches That Actually Fix It)
videoDescription: Struggling to sit cross-legged without your knees pointing at the ceiling? It's not just about flexibility—it's restricted hip rotation and tight muscles pulling back. Here are the four stretches that target the real problem, and how often you need to do them to see change. Full breakdown linked in bio.
script: If your knees stick up when you try to sit cross-legged, the problem isn't flexibility—it's restricted hip rotation. Your hip flexors, adductors, and external rotators are literally pulling back, keeping your thigh from rotating outward.

Four stretches actually fix this. Butterfly stretch for your inner thighs. 90/90 for both internal and external rotation—this one's key. Low lunge for hip flexors that get tight from sitting all day. And pigeon pose for your glutes and deep rotators.
The Mayo Clinic says you need at least two to three times a week for real flexibility gains—not once a week. Consistency beats duration. Ten minutes regularly will get you further than an hour once.
You should feel a stretch, not pain. Sharp pinching in your hip means you're pushing too hard. Over weeks, your knees will drop lower and cross-legged sitting will feel less like work.
The full breakdown of each stretch—with modifications if your hips don't reach the floor yet—is linked in the article.
